title: streaming: lifecycle controls for client cancel/disconnect/reconnect + server timeouts + OpenAI compat
author: Aisha Patel
release_notes: Add session resume tokens and reconnect window; resilient handling of client cancel/disconnect; server-side idle timeouts; OpenAI-compatible streaming events; docs and tests updated.
description:
Motivation: Streaming endpoints are fragile in the face of intermittent network issues and abrupt client-side cancellations. This PR introduces a set of lifecycle controls to make streaming sessions robust: explicit client cancel semantics, graceful handling of sudden disconnects with a configurable reconnect/resume window, and server-side idle/cleanup timeouts. It also updates the OpenAI compatibility layer so third-party clients can resume in a way consistent with upstream expectations.

What this changes (summary):
- Introduces a session manager that issues short-lived resume tokens on stream start. Resume tokens are opaque, single-use, and scoped to the stream/session.
- Client-cancel: clients can send an explicit cancel signal that immediately stops generation and returns a terminal event; server performs background cleanup while returning quick ack to the client.
- Disconnect/reconnect: if a client disconnects unexpectedly, the server retains the session state for a configurable reconnect_window (default 30s). Clients presenting a valid resume token can reconnect and receive the remaining stream.
- Server timeouts: configurable idle_timeout and max_resume_window enforced in runtime config; cleanup runs are offloaded to a background queue.
- OpenAI compatibility: streaming events include delta + done semantics, and a small compatibility shim maps Redwood resume semantics to an OpenAI-esque reconnect flow (resume_token + last_event_id).
- Observability: added metrics (stream.session_created, stream.session_resumed, stream.session_expired, stream.client_cancel) and traces for lifecycle transitions.
- Tests & docs: unit + integration tests cover cancel, disconnect/reconnect, and token expiry; docs updated with examples and SDK guidance.

Checklist: 
- [x] Implement session manager and resume token lifecycle
- [x] Server-side idle and resume window enforcement
- [x] OpenAI compatibility shim for resume events
- [x] SDK/handler updates and examples in docs
- [x] Unit and integration tests
- [x] Benchmarks: micro-bench to validate low-overhead for normal streams

Notes on backwards compatibility and rollout:
- Default behavior preserves current streaming semantics for clients that do not use resume: sessions still auto-cleanup after idle_timeout. No breaking change to the API contract; resume support is opt-in (clients must send resume_token).
- Config flags added to runtime config; rollout will be staged behind a feature flag and enabled by default for newer clusters after a rollout window.

Operational considerations:
- Memory cost: sessions held during reconnect_window are lightweight (KV cache handles pointers); added metric stream.session_mem_bytes to monitor.
- Security: resume tokens are HMACed and include a short expiry; rotation handled by key-service.

feat(streaming/openai_compat): add OpenAI-compatible resume event mapping
fix(streaming): immediate ack on client cancel, background cleanup
perf(streaming): make resume state allocation lazy to reduce overhead
test(streaming): add unit and integration tests for cancel/reconnect/expiry
docs(streaming): update streaming.md with examples and SDK notes
review_comments: Evan Cho: Overall looks good. Two requests: (1) make resume token single-use in the implementation (to avoid replay), and (2) add a metric for resume_rejects due to token expiry.

Aisha Patel: Addressed both. Resume tokens are now single-use via an atomic state transition, and added stream.resume_reject_expired metric. See commit feat(streaming): enforce single-use resume tokens and metrics.
Maya Li: Can you add a small benchmark to ensure normal non-resume streams don't regress on latency? Also please confirm memory footprint when many sessions are held during reconnect window.
Aisha Patel: Added micro-bench (ci/benchmarks/stream_latency_bench.py) and a lightweight mem metric (stream.session_mem_bytes). Benchmarks show <1% median latency regression under typical loads.
Jordan Kim: Nit: rename idle_timeout -> stream_idle_timeout in runtime config for clarity. Also update the config docs.\n\nRequested changes: rename applied and docs updated.
CI (automated): integration-tests initially failed due to flaky network in the test harness; rerun fixed the failure. All checks passed on Green build #7423.
